item: HCR-9 (steps 2 and 3: whole-memory rows, and the spaces re-measured on them)
space: Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-4B (full width 2560), entry rows = the whole memory file, cut at 1,024 tokens; body-chunk rows unchanged
machine: Apple Silicon (arm64 darwin, 128 GB), MLX in hippo's own venv, MLX buffer cache capped at 512 MB; fastembed bge-small-en-v1.5 for lean. The machine was under other load throughout (load average 50 to 260), so nothing here is a latency measurement.
method: bench/space_calibration.py: HCR-3's method (RET-1's recipe for the floor, HOT-2's gate, HOT-8's count rule, HOT-10's band), one space per process, every cell measured in explicit mode (recall()) and in hook mode (the real recall_hook.run_recall body, a fresh session per prompt; a hit is the expected memory on a rendered row). The MMR re-cut ran as it now ships (pool-scaled, lambda 0.4) in every cell except the floor sweep, which ran with it off.

corpora.golden: QUA-6 golden corpus, tests/golden_corpus (50 memories; 18 hard-set rows; 6 probes). Public.
corpora.packs: the starter-pack corpus CI seeds (22 memories; 32 rows; 6 probes). Public.
corpora.hippo: hippo's own corpus (108 memories): its 38 fixture rows, 11 fixture probes, plus HCR-8's 60 held-out questions. Private.
corpora.corpus-b: a private project corpus (113 memories): HCR-8's 80 held-out questions; no fixtures of its own. Nearly all of it is on the always-loaded floor, which the hook collapses onto one line, so its hook-mode hits read near zero on every arm and say nothing.
corpora.corpus-c: a private project corpus (1,070 memories): its own 104 fixture rows and 20 fixture probes, plus HCR-8's 207 held-out questions.
corpora.off_topic_probes: each corpus's own fixture probes, plus HCR-3's 12 generic and 12 adjacent technical probes on every corpus
corpora.replay: the 300 newest distinct human prompts of hippo's and of corpus-c's episode log, replayed through the hook on that corpus's copy: counts only

lean_arms.note: lean's own entries (floor 0.60, gate 0.76/0.72, count 0.05/0.18) in every cell; only the row text and the MMR re-cut differ

not_changed.BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5: keeps description rows and every entry it had. Whole-memory rows were measured on it (lean_arms) and not adopted: see the summary.
not_changed.Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-8B: keeps description rows and its HCR-3 entries. It was not re-measured; a model joins WHOLE_ROW_MODELS only with its own run of this bench.

summary: On whole-memory rows the 4B's classes sit where they sat, a little closer. Lowest on-topic best cosine 0.495 (0.495 on description rows); generic off-topic ceiling 0.4332 (was 0.402), now over the old 0.42 floor; the highest off-topic best of any kind 0.5549, from a 1,070-memory corpus's own probes and an adjacent technical probe on a web project's corpus, so the classes overlap on the two larger private corpora where they did not on the three corpora HCR-3 had.

Floor 0.42 -> 0.44: the low side of the generic gap again. It decides little. From 0.30 to 0.50 the five corpora find 481 to 484 of 539 on-topic rows, and with the gate on they abstain on the same probes at every floor; with the gate off almost nothing abstains at any floor. Against 0.42, in hook mode 0.44 finds 369 rows where 0.42 finds 368 and serves 8.66 rows per injecting replayed prompt where 0.42 serves 9.11 and 8.97.

Gate stays 0.60/0.60. 0.56/0.56 and 0.64/0.64 abstain on exactly the same probes. They differ on the replay: 0.56 injects on 236 and 241 of 300 prompts, 0.60 on 225 and 223, 0.64 on 222 and 217 (lean: 227 and 211); 0.64 costs 3 explicit rows.

Count rule stays 0.12/0.14, and it matters more than it did: against the rule off it finds 369 of 539 rows in hook mode where off finds 336 (a full block spends the render budget before the right row is rendered) and serves 137 rows on leaked probes where off serves 265. Entries near it (0.12/0.10, 0.08/0.14, 0.16/0.14, 0.20/0.14) read 367 to 371. A wider 'wide' trades rows served for rows found: 0.18 -> 363 found at 7.3 and 7.6 rows per injecting prompt; 0.22 -> 361 at 6.3 and 6.5; 0.26 -> 359 at 5.4 and 5.7; 0.30 -> 355 at 5.1 and 5.3. Lean serves 5.3 and 5.5.
Band default stands: 0 to 0.02 move two on-topic rows of 539 and no abstention.

As released, high against lean on the same 539 on-topic rows: explicit 482 against 438; hook 369 against 324. Injecting replayed prompts {'hippo': (225, 8.66), 'corpus-c': (219, 8.64)} against {'hippo': (227, 5.28), 'corpus-c': (211, 5.47)} (count, mean rows). Rows served on leaked probes: 137 against 100.

Abstention, explicit mode, probes abstained (fixture / generic / adjacent), high then lean: golden 5/12/12 vs 5/12/12; packs 6/11/11 vs 6/11/11; hippo 7/10/8 vs 7/10/11; corpus-b 0/11/7 vs 0/11/8; corpus-c 12/10/5 vs 15/7/5. High is behind lean on hippo's adjacent probes and corpus-c's own probes and ahead on corpus-c's generic ones; the same as on description rows (HCR-3 read 7/10/8 on hippo).

Lean on whole-memory rows, at lean's own entries: explicit 445 of 539 against 420 on description rows, hook 320 against 316, abstentions within one probe per class, the same replay volume. So whole rows help lean's plain recall (HCR-9's step 1 measured +0.043 [+0.014, +0.072] on the held-out set) and not what the hook serves. Its build is the cost: an unbudgeted build of the 1,070-memory corpus took 1,209 s on whole rows against 409 s on description rows on this machine (both under load), and the process held 11 GB. Not adopted in this release.
The MMR change alone, on lean: explicit 420 -> 438, hook 316 -> 324, abstentions identical.
caveats: Two of the five corpora and all the replayed prompts are private: counts and cosines only, no query and no memory name.
Held-out questions and their gold are a model's (HCR-8). Fixture rows are hand-written.
The replay has no labels: it counts prompts that got a block and rows served, not whether they were wanted.

The replay reads the 300 newest prompts at the time of each run, and both projects were in use, so the set drifts by a few prompts between runs (corpus-c's injecting count reads 219 to 223 for one setting across four runs).
Hook-mode hits depend on the render budget and the always-loaded floor, so they are comparable between arms on one corpus and not between corpora.

No interval is given on the calibration grids: each cell is one deterministic pass over fixed rows, and a difference of one to three rows between neighbouring cells is not a result. The profile comparison with intervals is in planning/HCR-9.tuned-lean.evidence.2026-11-27.json and planning/HCR-9.release.evidence.2026-11-27.json.
